headline: East 72 derives sum-of-parts valuation for EVT Limited, flagging significant undervaluation across cinema, German, and Thredbo assets
reasoning: Andrew Brown at East 72 conducts a detailed sum-of-parts analysis of EVT Limited, concluding it is materially undervalued. For the Australian cinema operations, using a per-screen valuation methodology similar to the mooted PEP/Hoyts transaction, he derives a value of ~A$670 million for the cinema business alone. The German Cinestar operations, including four owned properties, are valued at approximately A$128 million at ~8x EBIT plus property book value. Thredbo is valued between A$199 million (DCF) and A$281 million (property-backed), well above the A$113 million segmental book value. Collectively, the parts suggest EVT's intrinsic value significantly exceeds the market price, underpinned by a A$2.3 billion property portfolio announced in August 2025.
quote: Based on our crude adjustments to Event to evaluate 525 George Street, Sydney as a lease and ascribing an 11.5x EBIT multiple to forward earnings, we derive a low valuation of A$450million for the cinema operations; in a sale we view a per screen valuation as more useful suggesting a value of ~$670million. This lines up more closely with the mooted PEP offer for Hoyts.

headline: East 72 values EVT's German Cinestar cinema operations at ~A$128 million including owned properties, noting strong H1 FY26 rebound
reasoning: EVT acquired the remaining 50% of Kieft & Kieft (operator of the Cinestar circuit) in December 2023 after the business had declined to approximately breakeven. The German cinema business rebounded strongly in H1 FY26 driven by strong local film product, following two years of unprofitability. East 72 values the cinema operations at approximately A$60 million at ~8x EBIT, after adjusting for an imputed market rent on the four owned properties in Mainz, Düsseldorf, Stade and Neumünster, which were book-valued at A$68 million (7.3% yield). Total valuation is therefore approximately A$128 million with potential A$10–15 million upside from yield compression.
quote: The German business has rebounded strongly in H1FY26 on the back of strong local product, but over the preceding two years has not been profitable as a cinema operation. Income has effectively come from the ownership of four properties - 31 screens and related retail or hotel space – which were valued at $68million in the EVT property "book" in August 2025 – an effective yield of 7.3%, given the locations in Mainz, Dusseldorf, Stade and Neumunster. Adjusting cinema earnings for an effective rental if the properties were sold suggests the business to be worth ~A$60million at around 8x EBIT to give a total valuation around A$128million including property. There could reasonably be A$10-15million of upside from yield compression.

headline: Fundie backs EVT as a buy on asset backing close to current share price and hotel strategy shift towards asset-light model with near-term asset review catalysts
reasoning: EVT is an asset-heavy business exposed to hotels, cinemas and the Thredbo ski resort. The asset backing is approximately $11.70 per share and the stock trades at only a slight premium to that, meaning the market is essentially assigning no value to the operating business. The company is shifting its hotel division from asset-heavy to asset-light with a growing third-party management model. There are specific near-term catalysts including a review of 525 George Street and the QT precinct on George/Market Street in Sydney, with updates expected around August potentially involving JVs or asset sales. Cinema box office is also recovering with recent strong releases. These factors together represent meaningful upside from current levels.
quote: Highest conviction stock pick is EVT. So it's an asset heavy business that's exposed to hotels, cinemas and it also owns thread boat. So the asset backing on the stock is about $11.70 a share and it only trades at slight premium to that. So you're basically not paying for the operating business at the moment. The business is shifting on its hotel side from an asset heavy given that property backing towards more of an asset light model and improving return on investor capital going forward. And so we do see good upside from that hotel strategy going forward. The business is reviewing a number of its sites at the moment, including 525 George Street that we'll expect to see an update on in the next 46 weeks. That's an event, cinemas. That's right on George Street. They also own the QT precinct on George Street and Market Street. And that's another one that they expect to update around the August in terms of maybe a JV or plans for that site.
